hints.title: Palindrome Symmetry Construction
hints.text: A palindrome is determined by its first half, which mirrors directly onto the second half.

hints.title: Candidate Generation by Prefix
hints.text: Mirror the prefix of n + 1. If the mirrored candidate exceeds n, it is the minimal valid choice.

hints.title: Prefix Increment Handling
hints.text: If the direct reflection is less than or equal to n, increment the numeric prefix by one and mirror again.

hints.title: Reference Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def nextSpecialPalindrome(self, n: int) -> int:
        # Generate next palindrome strictly greater than n
        # Helper to check if string s is a palindrome
        cur = n + 1
        while True:
            s = str(cur)
            if s == s[::-1]:
                return cur
            # Speed up jump to next palindrome if needed
            half = len(s) // 2
            left = s[:len(s) - half]
            cand = int(left + left[::-1][len(s) % 2:])
            if cand > n:
                return cand
            cur = int(left) + 1
            cur = int(str(cur) + "0" * half)
```

variables: D: Number of digits in n
complexity.notes: Directly manipulates the upper half string of digits in linear time with respect to digit length.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Incrementing one by one could iterate through tens of thousands of numbers before encountering a palindrome.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Allocates string representation of length D to form mirrored halves.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Construct palindromes directly from the prefix rather than brute force scanning.
